items.bostonRelevance: Names New England shipbuilding and excellent harbors in the stimulus, which is the economic base Boston's port missions rest on.

stimulus.title: Cause-and-effect diagram
stimulus.text:
New England During the Colonial Period
• Depended on shipbuilding
• Had excellent harbors
→ (1)

The Mid-Atlantic During the Colonial Period
• Depended on farming
• Had rich, fertile soil
→ (2)
stimulus.note: Rendered as a two-row cause-and-effect diagram. Cell text captured verbatim; visual arrangement approximated.

items.stem: Which effects correctly replace the numbers in this cause-and-effect diagram?

options.text: (1) Used slave labor (2) Used Chinese laborers
(1) Exported dried fish (2) Exported agricultural goods
(1) Established plantations (2) Established textile factories
(1) Imported lumber (2) Imported cattle

items.optionTranscriptionNote: RECONSTRUCTED PAIRING, not a contiguous verbatim string. This is the only item in the dataset where that is true. TEA lays the four options out in two columns, so the PDF text layer interleaves them: line 1 is 'F (1) Used slave labor H (1) Established plantations', line 2 is '(2) Used Chinese laborers (2) Established textile factories', and so on. All eight fragments are individually verbatim from the source, and the column pairing is unambiguous (F and G occupy the left column, H and J the right), but each option's two halves were rejoined during transcription rather than copied as one run of text.

items.stem: Which statement describes BOTH the Free-Soil Party and the Republican Party in the mid-1800s?

options.text: They supported actions to stop escaped slaves from entering the North.
They supported enacting safety regulations to protect factory workers.
They were against the expansion of slavery into the western territories.
They were against the establishment of American Indian reservations.

items.bostonConcept: Boston Act 4 gated fact: Intolerable / Coercive Acts, including the Port Act closing the harbor

stimulus.title: The Daily Star (four mock headlines)
stimulus.text:
Great Britain Orders Closure of Boston Harbor Until Money Lost from Tea Is Repaid
Great Britain Dissolves Massachusetts Legislature
Great Britain Allows British Officials in America Charged with Crimes to Go to England for Trial
Great Britain Authorizes Colonial Governors to Quarter British Soldiers in Unoccupied Buildings
stimulus.note: Rendered as four mock newspaper mastheads. Headline text captured verbatim; the layout is not reproduced. The headlines are TEA-authored, not quotations from a real 1774 newspaper.

items.stem: How did the American colonists IMMEDIATELY respond to the 1774 laws described in these headlines?

options.text: The First Continental Congress declared war on Great Britain.
The colonists adopted the Articles of Confederation.
The First Continental Congress sent a list of grievances to King George III.
The colonists adopted the Bill of Rights.

items.bostonNote: Directly names the closure of Boston Harbor, the dissolved Massachusetts legislature, and quartering. This is the single best released item for Boston mission M11 (The Port Is Shut, 8.4(A) Intolerable Acts).

repoLinkage.relationship: The repo item is a condensed paraphrase of this released item and carries the same key (H). The repo's tag 8.4(A):INTOLERABLE_ACTS agrees with TEA's published label.
